bib.title: Adaptable Logical Control for Large Language Models

question: How can an LLM be made to follow arbitrary logical constraints at inference time with guaranteed satisfaction and without retraining per constraint?
hypothesis: A distilled HMM can approximate the LLM well enough, even at 7B scale, to guide generation toward DFA-specified constraints while keeping fluency.
contributions: Ctrl-G: distill an HMM from the LLM, specify constraints as DFAs, guide decoding with p_hmm(alpha | x_t, x_<t)
Exact O(nmh^2) algorithm for marginalising an HMM over any DFA constraint
Human evaluation on interactive text editing with TULU2-7B beating GPT3.5 and GPT4 on constraint satisfaction
Benchmarks on CommonGen and text infilling with GPT2 models; proof-of-concept on GSM

method.summary: Ctrl-G distills a Hidden Markov Model from a frozen LLM by training on unconditional LLM samples, compiles a logical constraint into a DFA, and at each decoding step multiplies the LLM next-token probability by the HMM's probability that the DFA will end in an accept state. Applied to GPT2-large/small for benchmarks and to a finetuned TULU2-7B for interactive text editing.
method.task: constrained text generation (keyphrase, word-length, infilling constraints)

datasets.name: CommonGen
datasets.size: 3 to 5 concepts per example; test size not stated
datasets.preprocessing: Aho-Corasick DFA per keyword over inflections, intersected across keywords

datasets.name: CommonGen+
datasets.preprocessing: 100 random 5-concept examples augmented with extra keywords sampled from reference sentences; 5 to 9 concepts

datasets.name: ROC stories text infilling (Donahue et al. 2020)
datasets.size: 4 test sets by masking ratio (13%, 21%, 32%, 40%); sizes not stated
datasets.source: Donahue, Lee, Liang 2020, based on ROC stories
datasets.preprocessing: mask function of Donahue et al. with changed hyperparameters

datasets.name: CoAuthor-based text editing set
datasets.source: CoAuthor (Lee et al. 2022); stories by humans and GPT3.5-turbo-instruct, ten topics
datasets.preprocessing: each story randomly split into prefix, infix, suffix; infix is gold reference; 1 to 3 keyphrases; length a to b words with 1<=a<=b<=32

datasets.name: WritingPrompt (Fan et al. 2018)
datasets.size: 3000 examples for TULU2 continuation finetune; 1000 examples for the insertion-finetuned baseline

datasets.name: GSM8K
datasets.size: 1319 test examples (293 subset where model skips numbers)

other.distillation_data: 5 million samples drawn from the finetuned TULU2-7B with prompt 'Continue the given text:'

other.finetune: 3000 WritingPrompt examples, prompt 'Continue the given text:'

training.objective: HMM trained on LLM samples to minimise KL divergence to the LLM (distillation)

other.note: HMM distillation follows Zhang et al. 2023 (GeLaTo); no optimizer, lr, steps or compute given here. TULU2 finetune on 3000 examples has no hyperparameters either.

inference.decoding: sample from p_ctrl-g(x_t | x_<t, alpha) proportional to p_lm * p_hmm(alpha | x_t, x_<t); 128 samples reranked by base-model likelihood, highest kept (text editing, all baselines too)
inference.samples: 128 per test example (text editing); ILM run 10 times; GSM: 16 outputs, majority vote
inference.prompting: TULU2 base sees 'Continue the given text:' plus prefix; for insertion the suffix is carried in the constraint, not the prompt. GPT models use OpenAI-docs-style templates (Table 5).

parameters.dfa_construction: KMP for single phrases, Aho-Corasick for inflection sets, intersection for AND, concatenation (Prop 4.1) for ordered fragments

other.gpt_sampling_settings: temperature and other API settings for GPT3.5/GPT4 not stated

metrics.name: Constraint satisfaction (Success)
metrics.definition: percentage of generations containing all required concepts / meeting keyphrase and length constraints

metrics.name: Quality
metrics.definition: human rating 1 to 5 on Q3 overall quality (Q1 fluency, Q2 coherency)

metrics.name: Overall satisfaction
metrics.definition: proportion of examples meeting logical constraints with Quality score above 3

eval.protocol: Human evaluation on MTurk: three annotators per example see all four models' outputs side by side, unaware of the constraints; Kendall's W averaged 0.449 (moderate). ILM mean and std over 10 runs. Single run for Ctrl-G otherwise; no significance tests.

results.claim: GSM proof of concept: forcing use of the problem's numbers lifts accuracy on the 293 hard examples to 28.3%, 3.4% higher than without.
results.setup: TULU2-7B, chain-of-thought, 16 samples majority vote, subset of 1319 where model skips given numbers
results.quote: with Ctrl-G, the model achieves 28.3% accuracy, which is 3.4% higher than the accuracy without Ctrl-G
results.note: baseline accuracy on the subset is not printed directly; implied 24.9 only by subtraction (inferred, 3.4 may be points or relative)

results.claim: Without Ctrl-G the model fails to use all numbers in 293 of 1319 GSM problems, and accuracy there is 14.6% vs 34.6% overall.
results.note: 14.6% on subset conflicts with the later 24.9% implied baseline for the same subset when majority vote of 16 is used; the 14.6% is likely a single-sample figure, paper does not say

results.claim: Time complexity of sampling n tokens is O(nmh^2) (m = DFA edges, h = HMM hidden states).
results.quote: the time complexity for sampling a sequence of n tokens from pctrl-g(x1:n | α) is O(nmh2)

results.claim: Per-token Ctrl-G overhead scales roughly linearly with DFA size and is constant in sequence length.
results.setup: Fig 6, A100 80GB, naive implementation, DFA size about 900 for the length sweep
results.quote: the generation time per token scales linearly w/ respect to DFA size

results.claim: Inter-annotator agreement is only moderate: Kendall's W averaged 0.449.
results.setup: MTurk human eval, 3 workers per item
results.quote: The average coefficient was 0.449, indicating a moderate level of agreement among the annotators.

limits: Constraints must be expressible as DFAs over a bounded-length token sequence; DFA concatenation can blow up exponentially, handled only in a special case (Prop 4.1).
An HMM must be distilled per base LLM (5M samples, 32768 states, ~2B params for the 7B model); needs access to logits and sampling, so it does not work through closed APIs.
Runtime numbers are from a naive implementation; authors leave efficiency to future work.
Human evaluators rated only fluency and coherence, not constraint compliance; agreement only moderate (W=0.449); no significance tests; GPT3.5/GPT4 versions and API settings not given.
Baselines are prompt-only GPT models; no comparison to API-level structured output or grammar-constrained decoding with a strong LLM.
GSM result is a small proof of concept on a self-selected 293-example subset.
Text editing evaluated on one domain (stories) and constraint family (keyphrase, word length).

terms.definition: framework that combines an LLM with a distilled HMM so outputs satisfy logical constraints given as DFAs

estimating how likely each next token is to eventually lead to the constraint being satisfied, rather than only discarding tokens that make it unsatisfiable (pure logical reasoning as in regex-based guidance)

lp = CtrlGLogitsProcessor(dfa, hmm, prefix, suffix)
llm.generate(logits_processor=lp)
